title: Proper/open interchange and its base-change and composition equations
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring. Use $D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$, the bounded-below derived category of constant-coefficient module sheaves on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], derived direct images [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], and exact extension by zero along open immersions [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]. For a commutative square
$$\begin{array}{ccc} A&\xrightarrow{k}&B\\ r\downarrow&&\downarrow p\\ C&\xrightarrow{i}&D\end{array}$$
with $p,r$ proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] and $k,i$ open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion], there is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$\gamma_Q:i_!Rr_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_*k_!.$$
No cartesian hypothesis is imposed. Its normalization on a K-injective representative $J$ of $K\in D^+(A_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ is the morphism represented by $i_!r_*J\cong p_*k_!J\to p_*I$, where $k_!J\to I$ is a K-injective resolution [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions]; the first identification is the canonical proper/open identification of sheaves. When $A=C$, $r=\mathrm{id}$, $k=j_1$, $i=j_2$ and $p=u$ with $uj_1=j_2$, this map equals $\alpha_u$ of [def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison].
For vertically stacked squares $Q_1,Q_2$ of this kind, with middle open $i_1$, bottom open $i_2$, left proper maps $r_1,r_2$, and right proper maps $p_1,p_2$, the equation is
$$\gamma_{Q_2Q_1}=(Rp_{2,*}\gamma_{Q_1})\circ(\gamma_{Q_2}Rr_{1,*}):i_{2!}Rr_{2,*}Rr_{1,*}\to Rp_{2,*}Rp_{1,*}k_{1!}.$$
For horizontally adjacent squares with left vertical $r$, middle vertical $p$, right vertical $q$, top opens $k,l$ and bottom opens $i,j$, the equation is
$$\gamma_{Q_2Q_1}=(\gamma_{Q_2}k_!)\circ(j_!\gamma_{Q_1}):j_!i_!Rr_*\to Rq_*l_!k_!,$$
All equations insert the canonical composition isomorphisms of direct images and extension by zero; squares whose two vertical maps are identities give identity comparisons, and squares whose two horizontal maps are identities give the identity on derived direct image.
Finally, let $b:D_1\to D$ be any morphism, let $Q_1$ be the base change of $Q$ by $b$, and write $a:B_1\to B$, $c:C_1\to C$, $d:A_1\to A$ for projections. Let $\beta_i:b^{-1}i_!\cong i_{1!}c^{-1}$ and $\beta_k:a^{-1}k_!\cong k_{1!}d^{-1}$ be the extension-by-zero base-change maps [cor-cbc-derived-extension-zero-base-change], and let $\operatorname{Ex}_r:c^{-1}Rr_*\to Rr_{1,*}d^{-1}$ and $\operatorname{Ex}_p:b^{-1}Rp_*\to Rp_{1,*}a^{-1}$ be the module exchange maps [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients]. Then
$$ (Rp_{1,*}\beta_k)\circ(\operatorname{Ex}_p k_!)\circ(b^{-1}\gamma_Q)
=(\gamma_{Q_1}d^{-1})\circ(i_{1!}\operatorname{Ex}_r)\circ(\beta_iRr_*). $$ Base changes here are formed by fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product].

proof.text:
Write $h=ir=pk$. Proper maps are separated and of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism], hence locally of finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. An open immersion identifies its source with an open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion]; its diagonal is an isomorphism, hence a closed immersion, and locally on that open subscheme its ring map is the identity, a finite-type map. Thus the separated and locally finite-type hypotheses of [lem-cbc-proper-support-sheaf-composition] hold. That node gives, for every module sheaf $F$ on $A$, the canonical identification
$$\delta_Q(F):i_!r_*F=i_!^{\mathrm{supp}}r_!^{\mathrm{supp}}F=h_!^{\mathrm{supp}}F=p_!^{\mathrm{supp}}k_!^{\mathrm{supp}}F=p_*k_!F.$$
All the equalities mean the same subsheaf of $h_*F$: a section is carried to the same section, rather than to an arbitrary abstract isomorphism. Thus $\delta_Q$ is natural and $\Lambda$-linear, and extends degreewise to complexes. For successive squares, all identifications of the underlying sheaves are identities on these common sections. In particular the sheaf versions of both stated composition equations hold. The proper-support composition result applies without Cartesian or quasi-compact-open assumptions.

proof.text: Choose a universe in which the small etale sites are small. By [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] their constant-ring module-sheaf categories are Grothendieck abelian. They have enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]. Represent $K$ by a bounded-below complex $J$ of injective module sheaves using [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative], and choose a bounded-below injective resolution $t:k_!J\to I$. Exactness [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact] makes $k_!J$ a bounded-below representative of $k_!K$. Each $k_!J^n$ is $p_*$-acyclic by [lem-cbc-open-extended-injective-proper-acyclic]. Clause (3) of [lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity] therefore says that $p_*t:p_*k_!J\to p_*I$ is a quasi-isomorphism and computes the derived-functor comparison. Since $r_*J$ computes $Rr_*K$ by [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], the composite $i_!r_*J\xrightarrow{\delta_Q}p_*k_!J\xrightarrow{p_*t}p_*I$ gives the required isomorphism. Finite $\Lambda$ is torsion: multiplying positive integers annihilating its finitely many additive elements gives $N>0$ with $N\Lambda=0$, hence $NM=0$ for every $\Lambda$-module $M$. This is precisely case (b) of 0F7B, with no residue-characteristic restriction.

source.place: Tag 0F7B, case (b); derived.tex bounded-below acyclic-complex computation

proof.text: Morphisms into a K-injective complex are uniquely represented up to homotopy by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. Given any other K-injective representative $J'$ of $K$, its identification with $J$ lifts to a homotopy equivalence. Applying the additive functors $i_!r_*$ and $p_*k_!$ preserves that homotopy equivalence. Write $h:J\to J'$ for this homotopy equivalence and $t:k_!J\to I$, $t':k_!J'\to I'$ for the resolutions. The derived morphism $Q(t')\circ Q(k_!h)\circ Q(t)^{-1}:QI\to QI'$ lifts to a chain map $u:I\to I'$ by the Hom bijection. Since $I'$ is K-injective, equality of the derived classes of $ut$ and $t'k_!h$ gives the homotopy $ut\simeq t'k_!h$. Naturality of $\delta_Q$ makes the corresponding comparison diagram commute up to homotopy, and applying $p_*$ preserves the homotopy. The resulting derived arrow is independent of all these choices and is natural in $K$, again by the Hom bijection. This also proves the stated normalization for any K-injective representative, even if it is not itself bounded below termwise. Exactness of $k_!$ is used to descend it through localization; no claim that $k_!$ preserves injectives is made.

source.place: Tag 0F7B, construction with K-injectives and naturality of its canonical map

proof.text: In the refinement case use [def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison]. Its construction identifies $V=u^{-1}(j_2(X))$ and its clopen component $s(X)$, with $bs=j_1$, $ps=\mathrm{id}_X$. Restrict the arrow just constructed to $j_2$. Under the restriction isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-derived-open-restriction], the extension-by-zero comparison [cor-cbc-derived-extension-zero-base-change], and the component restriction [lem-weil-pbc-clopen-section-direct-image], its source and target become $K$. The underived $\delta$ sends a section on $X$ to itself on $s(X)$ and zero on the other component. Thus this restricted arrow is exactly $\theta_{u,K}^{-1}$ from the comparison definition; the resolution map is the canonical derived comparison and does not change that identity on the component. The adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction], descended degreewise since extension by zero and inverse image are exact [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact] [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], makes the arrow $j_{2!}K\to Ru_*j_{1!}K$ uniquely determined by this restriction. It is consequently $\alpha_{u,K}$, the adjoint of $\theta_{u,K}^{-1}$.

source.place: Tag 0F7B, specialization to a refinement; comparison definition and its component normalization

proof.text:
For vertically stacked $Q_1,Q_2$, choose $J$ bounded-below injective on the upper-left scheme and $t:k_{1!}J\to I$ bounded-below injective on the upper-right scheme. Direct image preserves injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-direct-image-preserves-injectives], so $r_{1,*}J$ and $p_{1,*}I$ are bounded-below injective complexes. Put $E=i_{1!}r_{1,*}J$ and $a=p_{1,*}t\circ\delta_{Q_1}:E\to p_{1,*}I$. This is a quasi-isomorphism by step 2. For $Q_2$, every term of $E$ is $p_{2,*}$-acyclic by [lem-cbc-open-extended-injective-proper-acyclic], applied to the injective terms of $r_{1,*}J$. Clause (3) of [lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity] shows that $E$ computes $Rp_{2,*}E$; thus $Rp_{2,*}(\gamma_{Q_1})$ is represented by $p_{2,*}a$. The two-square composite is represented by
$$i_{2!}r_{2,*}r_{1,*}J\xrightarrow{\delta_{Q_2}}p_{2,*}i_{1!}r_{1,*}J\xrightarrow{p_{2,*}a}p_{2,*}p_{1,*}I.$$
Step 1 identifies this composite with $\delta_{Q_2Q_1}$ followed by $(p_2p_1)_*t$. The compositor [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] is normalized on these injective direct images with the identity as the extra resolution. Consequently these are exactly the representatives of the displayed vertical equation, with the canonical compositors inserted.

source.place: Tag 0F7C, label lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-compose, full resolution calculation

proof.text:
For horizontal composition choose bounded-below injective $J$ on the left, $t:k_!J\to I$ in the middle, and $v:l_!I\to L$ on the right. By [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact], $w=v\circ l_!t:l_!k_!J\to L$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The two-square comparison is represented by
$$j_!i_!r_*J\xrightarrow{j_!(p_*t\circ\delta_{Q_1})}j_!p_*I\xrightarrow{q_*v\circ\delta_{Q_2}}q_*L.$$
Naturality of the sheaf identification $\delta_{Q_2}$ moves $t$ through it. The sheaf composition equality in step 1 then makes this map $q_*w\circ\delta_{Q_2Q_1}$, the representative for the outer rectangle. The identification $j_!i_!\cong(ji)_!$ is the sheaf support-composition equality in [lem-cbc-proper-support-sheaf-composition], applied degreewise; its exactness just cited lets it descend to $D^+$. This proves the stated horizontal equation. For horizontal identities take $t=\mathrm{id}_J$; $\delta$ is the identity and one obtains the identity on derived pushforward. For vertical identities $k=i$ and $p=r=\mathrm{id}$, so the constructed arrow is the quasi-isomorphism $k_!J\to I$, which represents the identity of $k_!K$.

For base change first work with sheaves. The support inclusions into ordinary direct images in [lem-cbc-proper-support-sheaf-composition] identify $i_!r_*$ and $p_*k_!$ inside $(ir)_*=(pk)_*$. Its pullback-composition clause says that the two paths consisting of the ordinary comparisons and the extension-by-zero comparisons give the pullback comparison for that same composite morphism. Thus the ordinary version of the required base-change diagram commutes. More explicitly, after inclusion into $(p_1k_1)_*d^{-1}F=(i_1r_1)_*d^{-1}F$, either path pulls a local section of $F$ to the same section on the base-changed test scheme. These are injective inclusions; inverse image preserves them by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Hence equality in the common ordinary direct image is equality in the support subsheaf. The open comparisons here are the specific $\beta_i,\beta_k$ of [cor-cbc-derived-extension-zero-base-change], not isomorphisms chosen independently of the pullback maps. Their construction is the restriction of the ordinary pullback comparison to the support subsheaf. The ordinary-comparison pasting is also the unit/counit mate equation in clauses (1),(2) of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] for the module inverse-image adjunctions; all constant-ring pullbacks are the identifications of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact].

proof.text:
Now take $J,t:k_!J\to I$ as in step 2, and choose a bounded-below injective resolution $s:d^{-1}J\to J_1$. Exact inverse image and exact extension by zero [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact] make the diagram start with quasi-isomorphisms
$$k_{1!}d^{-1}J\xrightarrow{k_{1!}s}k_{1!}J_1,\qquad
k_{1!}d^{-1}J\xrightarrow{\beta_k^{-1}}a^{-1}k_!J\xrightarrow{a^{-1}t}a^{-1}I.$$
Choose a bounded-below injective resolution $v:k_{1!}J_1\to I_1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], the morphism from $a^{-1}I$ to $I_1$ corresponding in the derived category to $v\circ k_{1!}s\circ\beta_k\circ(a^{-1}t)^{-1}$ is represented by a chain map $z:a^{-1}I\to I_1$. It satisfies
$$z\circ a^{-1}t\circ\beta_k^{-1}\simeq v\circ k_{1!}s,$$
because the maps from $k_{1!}d^{-1}J$ into the K-injective $I_1$ have the same derived class. This is the needed homotopy-commutative resolution diagram, not a claim that $d^{-1}J$ or $a^{-1}I$ is injective. The module exchange maps are represented by the ordinary comparisons $b^{-1}p_*I\to p_{1,*}a^{-1}I$ followed by $p_{1,*}z$, and $c^{-1}r_*J\to r_{1,*}d^{-1}J$ followed by $r_{1,*}s$. To verify this computation rather than take it from a definition, use the exact module adjunction of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], its termwise adjunction on homotopy categories [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy], and the K-injective Hom bijection. Exactness of inverse image shows its additive right adjoint preserves K-injectives: if $H$ is acyclic and $P$ is K-injective, $\operatorname{Hom}_K(H,p_*P)=\operatorname{Hom}_K(p^{-1}H,P)=0$. Thus the two homotopy-category Hom sets in this adjunction identify with the corresponding derived Hom sets for injective target resolutions, with the same counit represented by $\varepsilon_{p,P}$. For a source representative $P$ and a target resolution $z:a^{-1}P\to I_1$, the transpose of $p_{1,*}z\circ\operatorname{Ex}^0_P$ is the chain map $z\circ a^{-1}\varepsilon_{p,P}\circ\theta$, by the defining adjoint formula of [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange] and the underived adjunction triangle identities. That formula is stated for abelian sheaves; [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] gives exactly those same units and counits on constant-ring modules, and its section-restriction maps are linear, so the displayed formula is the module formula too. Maps into $I_1$ are computed modulo homotopy by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], so this is also its derived transpose. This is exactly the defining derived mate in [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange], formed for module adjunctions as specified in [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients]. For the left proper map, the chain map $r_{1,*}s\circ\operatorname{Ex}^0_{r,J}$ has transpose $s\circ d^{-1}\varepsilon_{r,J}\circ\theta_r:r_1^{-1}c^{-1}r_*J\to J_1$. The termwise adjunction and the Hom bijection into $J_1$ identify this transpose with the derived composite $d^{-1}\varepsilon_r\circ\theta_r$ followed by the resolution identification. Hence this chain map represents $\operatorname{Ex}_r$. No module computation is being inferred from the abelian-only termwise-exchange theorem. Apply the ordinary equality of step 7 degreewise to $J$. Naturality of $\delta_{Q_1}$ with respect to $s$ gives equality for the next segment. For the last segment apply $p_{1,*}$ to the displayed homotopy: it remains a homotopy since direct image is additive. The outside paths are therefore equal in the homotopy category after passing through $p_{1,*}I_1$, and hence in $D^+$. Written using the normalization of step 2 these paths are exactly
$$(Rp_{1,*}\beta_k)\circ(\operatorname{Ex}_p k_!)\circ(b^{-1}\gamma_Q)
=(\gamma_{Q_1}d^{-1})\circ(i_{1!}\operatorname{Ex}_r)\circ(\beta_iRr_*).$$
Properness and openness in $Q_1$ hold by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change], respectively. Thus all comparisons used here are of the stated kind for arbitrary $b$. The exchanges stay in the constant-$\Lambda$ module categories; the comparison [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients] identifies their underlying abelian exchanges but is not used to infer equality from derived forgetting.
